rounds.text: Amal Ltd is demonstrating a powerful operational acceleration, highlighted by a staggering 73% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a quarterly net profit surge of 1179% year-on-year [E11, E59]. Quarterly operating margins have expanded dramatically to 14% in June 2026 compared to just 4% in the same quarter of the previous year, driven by higher price realization and improved capacity utilization [E24, E72]. The company operates from a position of absolute financial strength with a zero debt-to-equity ratio and capital expenditure underway through two active growth proposals alongside a massive 1116% surge in capital work-in-progress [E31, E33, E73]. Furthermore, the broader chemicals sector provides a supportive macro backdrop with a strong tailwind score of 0.77, while management has successfully wiped out its historical carried-forward losses and built a clean operational foundation [E66, E79]. Conceded: [E37], the static discounted cash flow model suggests overvaluation and the historical return on equity remains subdued at 5% over the medium term [E21, E37].

Amal Ltd trades at a prohibitive valuation that is entirely decoupled from its historical operating performance, carrying a P/E multiple of 138x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 9.39x [E2]. This extreme multiple is levied on a business with mediocre historical returns, posting a 5-year median return on equity of just 5% [E20] and a TTM ROCE of only 7.1% [E6]. The underlying fundamental reality offers zero support for these metrics, as demonstrated by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value calculation of Rs 61 per share against a market price of Rs 756 [E37], resulting in a staggering margin of safety deficit of -1145.3% [E38]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months reached 73% [E11]. Furthermore, cash generation is deeply concerning, with a cash conversion ratio of just 0.04x for March 2026 where operating cash flows collapsed to Rs 0.16 Cr against reported profits [E27, E28], leaving the company burning free cash flow at Rs -6.08 Cr [E29]. Finally, the reverse DCF indicates that today's market price aggressively demands a sustained 35.3% earnings growth rate [E39], setting an impossibly high hurdle for a company whose 5-year compounded profit growth actually sits at -13% [E13].

Conceded: [E1] and [E2]. However, focusing solely on high trailing multiples ignores a powerful and accelerating fundamental turnaround that makes historical averages obsolete [E65]. Compounded sales growth has scaled aggressively, hitting 23% over 5 years, 29% over 3 years, and an extraordinary 73% over the trailing twelve months [E9, E10, E11], driven by higher price realisation and capacity utilisation [E72]. Conceded: [E13] and [E37]. Yet, quarterly momentum has completely shifted as operating margin expanded by 9 percentage points to 14% in June 2026 compared to 4% in the year-ago quarter [E24], producing a massive net profit surge of 1179% year-on-year [E59]. Conceded: [E27] and [E29]. On the balance sheet front, the company is entirely debt-free with borrowings of zero [E31, E32], having successfully wiped out its historical carried-forward losses [E79], while actively channeling growth spend into an 1116% surge in capital work-in-progress [E33] alongside active capacity-upgrade projects [E73]. Finally, the chemical sector operates under a strong macro tailwind [E66] and the company boasts a stellar relative-strength rating of 94 against the Nifty 500 [E43], confirming that institutional price momentum and operating tailwinds strongly favor the ongoing structural inflection rather than backward-looking metrics [E65].
